engine: Nunjucks (server-side). Form-field values are typed { type:"FIXED"|"EXPRESSION", value }. ONLY type=EXPRESSION values are evaluated. A closing }} auto-gets `| json | safe`.
source: VERIFIED from workflow-automation-worker/controllers/execute.js (node_prototype, parseExpression, latest_node_data/all_node_data build ~L342-586), lib/sandbox_v2.js (code-node context), workflow-builder-trigger-handler (trigger execution_data), AND real captured workflows in mcp-server/captures.

core_model.wrapper: Every node stores its output as execution_data = { node: { node_name, node_uid, ... }, data: <payload> }. EVERY accessor ($item, $.getLatestNodeData(), $.getNodeData()[i], $.getRecentNodeData()) returns this WRAPPER object — NOT the bare payload.
core_model.golden_rule: ALWAYS reach a field through `.data`:  <accessor>.data.<...path...>. Omitting `.data` is the #1 cause of broken workflows.
core_model.node_name_is_display_name: The name passed to getNodeData/getLatestNodeData is the node's DISPLAY NAME (action_name), e.g. 'On Webhook', 'Get Record', 'Code'. Node names are unique per workflow (the backend enforces it), so named access is stable.
core_model.verified_real_form: {{$.getNodeData('On Webhook')[0]['data']['body']['date']}}  — note [0] (run index) then ['data'] then the payload path.

accessors.returns: the LATEST single wrapper of that node → .data is its payload
accessors.use: RECOMMENDED default. Named + robust to graph reordering. e.g. {{ $.getLatestNodeData('Get Record').data.data.work_order_number }}

accessors.returns: ARRAY of wrappers (one per run; multiple when the node is inside a loop). [0] = first run.
accessors.use: When you need a specific run or all runs of a node. e.g. {{ $.getNodeData('On Webhook')[0].data.body.job_uid }}

accessors.returns: the IMMEDIATELY-PREVIOUS node's wrapper → .data is its payload
accessors.use: Quick access to the node right before this one. Equivalent to getLatestNodeData of the previous node. e.g. {{ $item.data.body.job_uid }} (when the previous node is the webhook trigger). PREFER named access for clarity in multi-node flows.
accessors.warning: $item is POSITIONAL — it changes if the graph is reordered. It is the WRAPPER, so you still need .data.

accessors.returns: the n-th previous node's wrapper (1..100); 0/empty = latest (== $item)
accessors.use: Walk back N nodes along the prev_execution chain.

accessors.returns: a company workflow variable value (top-level — NOT through .data)

trigger_data_shapes.note: What the TRIGGER node's wrapper.data contains, by trigger type (verified).

external_webhook.note: The incoming request body is under .data.body — NOT .data directly.

zuper_event.note: Event payload (the job/customer/etc.) is under .data.body. For full entity fields not in the event, add a Zuper Get Record node and read .data.data from it.

schedule.note: Schedule triggers carry timing/context, not an entity.

node_output_shapes.note: What each ACTION node's wrapper.data contains (verified from captures + worker code). Mind the DOUBLE-`data` cases.

zuper_get_record.data_shape: { data: { <full Zuper entity> }, ... }  ← Zuper API response stored verbatim
zuper_get_record.gotcha: custom_fields is an ARRAY indexed by position (['14']), each { label, value, ... }.

http_request_v2.data_shape: { http_status, status, data: <response body>, headers, request_data }
http_request_v2.access: response body at .data.data ; HTTP status code at .data.status ; SUCCESS/ERROR at .data.http_status
http_request_v2.gotcha: DOUBLE data again — the HTTP response body lives at wrapper.data.data.

code.note: If your code returns { items, a, b }, access them as .data.items / .data.a / .data.b. v2 code reads inputs via $input.<name>; v1 via $/$item.

if_else.note: Routing is by output_value (TRUE→two-a, FALSE→two-b). You rarely read its data; read the upstream node it tested.

loop.data_shape: per-iteration: wrapper.data = the CURRENT array element; wrapper also carries current_iteration / total_iterations / overall_data at the TOP level.
loop.note: See `loop` section for the proper accessors.

loop.use: current iteration, 0-based; null if not in a loop
total iterations; null if not in a loop
the full array the loop iterates over
boolean — is the current node inside a loop body
inside a loop body, $item is usually the loop's current element wrapper → .data is the element

loop.note: Inside a loop, $.getNodeData('<node in body>') returns an ARRAY across iterations — use [$.getCurrentLoopIndex()] or [i] to pick one.

variables.note: Variables are top-level (no .data). Provision new ones with the create_variable MCP tool; secrets → is_sensitive (masked on read, still usable in expressions).

rendering.json_safe: Closing }} auto-gets `| json | safe`, so {{ $.getLatestNodeData('Code').data.items }} renders the object/array correctly. Only add `| json | safe` manually when you MIX literal text with an object in one field.
rendering.bracket_vs_dot: Both notations work: .data.body.job_uid  ==  ['data']['body']['job_uid']. Use brackets for numeric/odd keys: .data.data.custom_fields['14'].value or [14].
rendering.js_in_expression: Nunjucks evaluates JS-ish expressions: {{ $item.data.amount > 1000 ? 'high':'low' }}, {{ moment($item.data.created_at).format('YYYY-MM-DD') }} (moment available in code nodes).

fixed_vs_expression.rule: A field value is { type, value }. type='EXPRESSION' → the value is Nunjucks-evaluated against { $, $item, variable, VARIABLE }. type='FIXED' → used literally (even if it contains {{ }}).
fixed_vs_expression.implication: Any value that references upstream data MUST be type='EXPRESSION'. A literal UID/string/number is type='FIXED'.

notification_body_dual_templating.note: In email/notification SUBJECT and BODY (type=EXPRESSION) two syntaxes coexist (renderTemplatePreservingHandlebars, zuper worker):
notification_body_dual_templating.workflow_expression: {{ $... }} (starts with $) → evaluated by Nunjucks. e.g. {{ $.getLatestNodeData('Get Record').data.data.customer.email }}
notification_body_dual_templating.zuper_handlebars: {{ <non-$ merge tag> }} → PRESERVED and resolved later by Zuper. e.g. {{ customer.first_name }}, {{ job.job_number }}
notification_body_dual_templating.rule: If the inside of {{ }} begins with $ (or variable/VARIABLE) it is a workflow expression; otherwise it is a Zuper handlebars merge-tag passed through untouched.

common_mistakes: OMITTING .data — wrong: {{ $item.body.job_uid }} / {{ $item.job_uid }} ; right: {{ $item.data.body.job_uid }}. Every accessor returns the {node,data} wrapper.
Forgetting the DOUBLE data on Get Record / HTTP — right: {{ $.getLatestNodeData('Get Record').data.data.work_order_number }} and {{ $.getLatestNodeData('HTTP Request').data.data.<field> }}.
Reading webhook fields without .body — webhook payload is at .data.body.<field> (also .query/.headers/.params).
Using $.getNodeData('X') without an index — it returns an ARRAY; use [0] (or the loop index).
Referencing a node by a wrong/duplicate display name — names must be unique; use the exact action_name.
Putting a data expression in a type='FIXED' field — it won't be evaluated; use type='EXPRESSION'.
Guessing entity field paths — confirm real field names from the actual upstream execution_data / a Get Record output, not assumptions.

worked_examples.note: or {{ $item.data.body.job_uid }} if On Webhook is the immediately previous node
